SECTION: PREMIER SCHOLARS PROGRAMMES (Pages 7-9)

TOPICS: Renaissance Engineering Programme, NTU-University Scholars Programme, CN Yang Scholars Programme, NTU-NIE Teaching Scholars Programme, Undergraduate Research Experience on Campus, Minor Programmes

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The Renaissance Engineering Programme (REP) is a four-and-a-half-year dual-degree programme that awards a Bachelor of Engineering Science from the College of Engineering and a Master of Science in Technology Management from the Nanyang Business School (Page 7)
- REP scholars must complete a mandatory one-year Professional Attachment in the United States, Europe, or Singapore (Page 7)
- The NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP) aims to develop independent thinkers and empathetic leaders with a global mindset through an interdisciplinary curriculum (Page 7)
- NTU-USP features include a semester-long Study Abroad programme, an overseas student symposium, and a week-long overseas research under a Fieldwork and Documentation module (Page 7)
- The CN Yang Scholars Programme (CNYSP) nurtures future leaders at the interface of science and engineering, focusing on technological innovation and scientific communication (Page 8)
- CNYSP provides skills in research, making-and-tinkering, academic writing, and communication, and offers research attachment opportunities from Year 1, financial support for overseas projects, and an option to pursue postgraduate study (PhD) (Page 8)
- The NTU-NIE Teaching Scholars Programme (TSP) augments the four-year Double Major Programme to nurture well-rounded educators, focusing on content mastery, pedagogical knowledge, and the theory-practice nexus (Page 8)
- TSP features academic and educational research, dedicated academic advisors, opportunities for Masters level courses, and a minor in a second academic subject (Page 8)
- The URECA programme runs for one academic year from August to June and is available to undergraduates from 2nd year onwards who meet eligibility requirements (Page 9)
- The programme aims to foster a university-wide research culture and develop research capabilities (Page 9)
- There are more than 45 minors available for students to choose from, allowing them to broaden their knowledge and acquire diverse skills beyond their disciplines (Page 9)

This page (Pages 6-7) introduces NTU's "Nurturing Talent for the Good" initiative, which aims to foster holistic education by empowering students to develop skills in service of societal betterment. The left side details two key programmes: the NTU Talent Scholarship (TS), offering financial benefits like full tuition coverage and a $6,500 living allowance, and the NTU Student Talent Development Programme (STDP), which helps students hone their skills and connect with relevant industries. The right side presents five distinct undergraduate pathways under the theme "Which NTU Undergraduate Are You?", including Tech Disruptor, Eco Champion, Innovation Entrepreneur, Wellbeing & Healthcare Advocate, and Culture & Society Specialist, each with a unique focus area.

**Text Evidence:**
- NTU fosters an environment that promotes learning and empowers students to nurture their skills for the good.
- Students will learn to STAND OUT, have a strong sense of purpose to STAND UP for causes, and develop a STANDPOINT to build, unite, and heal.
- The NTU Talent Scholarship (TS) provides full coverage of subsidised tuition fees, a living allowance of S$6,500 per academic year, and accommodation allowance of up to S$2,000 per academic year.
- The NTU Student Talent Development Programme (STDP) empowers students to hone their skills and offers curated programmes to develop competencies relevant to their advocacies.
- Five undergraduate pathways are offered: Tech Disruptor, Eco Champion, Innovation Entrepreneur, Wellbeing & Healthcare Advocate, and Culture & Society Specialist.

pages.ocr_text: STUDENTupport NTU LIBRARY NTU Library's seven libraries at the Yunnan Garden campus provide access to a variety of resources, facilities and services for your study, research and wellbeing needs. At our libraries, you can find: Library Resources & Services Highlights IT SERVICES NTU's advanced suite of IT services are available to help you stay connected, learn more effectively and live more comfortably. ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT You can book an appointment with One Stop@sAC for administrative and finance-related queries and requests. The services include collection of certificates, concession and matriculation card, payment matters, endorsement of certificates and documents to update residence status, among many others. UNIVERSITY WELLBEING NTU adopts a campus community approach to student support and care, which entails departments, offices, schools, and halls working closely together to address the wellbeing needs of everyone on campus. Our University Wellbeing Office (UWO) is the central care and support provider and coordinator for students and employees. UWO focuses on four essential areas—counselling services, proactive & preventive programming, critical care and first responder support, as well as workplace wellbeing—to promote and ensure a balanced university life for all. Services include: STUDENTS WITH SPECIAL NEEDS Committed to fostering an inclusive campus community, NTU offers a wide range of services to support students with special needs. 4 The Peer Helping Programme (PHP) has allowed me to gain a deeper understanding of mental health and wellbeing issues which are not usually openly talked about. Being able to go on this journey with like-minded individuals has been profoundly heartening. And it has motivated me to work with my peers to improve the mental health space for students at NTU. LOW ZHIN XUAN ASHELY 44 Thanks to the befriending sessions in the Peer Helping Programme (PHP), I had the opportunity to connect with peers from various backgrounds who share a mutual passion for raising awareness about mental health issues. What an incredible way to cultivate empathy and learn how to listen more actively. — LIM JING WEE

pages.ocr_text: BE AN NTU SCHOLAR! Maximise your potential and make the most of your university education by applying for any of the various NTU scholarships. As an NTU Scholar, you will gain an edge as you navigate student life, pursue your passions and grow to be a game-changer in school, at work and in the community. The Renaissance Engineering Programme (REP) Scholarship, NTU-University Scholars Programme (NTU-USP) Scholarship and the CN Yang Scholars Programme (CNYSP) Scholarship are three of the most prestigious scholarships in NTU. These scholarships provide generous financial coverage and exclusive non-financial benefits such as multidisciplinary learning opportunities, guaranteed accommodation at NTU and placements in overseas programmes during your undergraduate years. It emphasizes that scholarships are applied for through the same portal as admissions, with shared deadlines, and directs readers to a table on pages 46-47 for more details. This page provides information on applying to Nanyang Technological University (NTU), focusing on Aptitude-Based Admissions (ABA) and the Adult Learners Scheme (ALS). It outlines application requirements, including academic qualifications, essays, and interviews. The main content is a detailed table listing application periods and fees for various applicant groups, such as those with Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' Level, Diploma from a polytechnic, NUS High School Diploma, International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, and Part-Time B.Eng or B.Tech programs. The page also includes notes clarifying eligibility for former/current students of other universities and NTU.

**Text Evidence:**
- NTU prioritizes aptitude beyond academic scores through its Aptitude-Based Admissions (ABA).
- ABA requires a minimum academic competence, a 500-word essay, 1-2 online appraisals, and an interview.
- The Adult Learners Scheme (ALS) is for working adults with at least 4 years of work experience or being 25 years old.
- Application periods and fees vary by qualification type, with specific dates like 1 Feb 2024 to 21 Feb 2024 for diploma holders and 3 Nov 2023 to 15 Jan 2024 for Part-Time B.Eng.
- Application fees are S$15 for Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents and S$25 for international applicants for most programs, except S$65 for Part-Time B.Tech in Computing.

**Visual Evidence:**
